title: U.S. House · Missouri's 2nd District
area: Western St. Louis County and St. Charles County suburbs, including Chesterfield, Ballwin, Wildwood and St. Charles.

context.text: Incumbent Ann Wagner won the August 4, 2026 Republican primary over Matthew Grant, Peter Pfeifer, Elizabeth Sparks-Holmes and Brandon Wilkinson. Frederick Wellman won the Democratic primary over Timothy D. Bilash and Joan VonDras. Brandon Daugherty advanced unopposed in the Libertarian primary.

candidates.name: Ann Wagner

summary.text: Ann Wagner is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Missouri's 2nd District. A former U.S. Ambassador to Luxembourg and Missouri Republican Party chair, she chairs the House Financial Services Committee.

background.text: Graduated from the University of Missouri-Columbia Business School in 1984 with a degree in business administration, specializing in logistics; worked in management for Hallmark and Ralston-Purina.
Served as the first woman to chair the Missouri Republican Party (1999-2005) and as co-chair of the Republican National Committee (2001-2005).
Served as U.S. Ambassador to Luxembourg from 2005 to 2009.

priorities.text: Lists budget and spending, the economy and jobs, defense and national security, energy, and veterans issues among her legislative priorities.

positions.summary: Says the U.S. should fully cultivate domestic oil resources by ending drilling moratoriums and increasing onshore and offshore production rather than relying on oil imports.

record.text: Chairs the House Committee on Financial Services in the 119th Congress (2025-2026); also serves on the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, chairing its Open Source Intelligence Subcommittee.

candidates.name: Frederick Wellman

summary.text: Frederick (Fred) Wellman is the Democratic nominee for Missouri's 2nd District. A retired Army helicopter pilot and 20-year veteran who later led the Lincoln Project, he is campaigning on affordability, healthcare and retirement security.

background.text: Grew up in Kirkwood, Missouri; attended West Point and served more than 20 years in the U.S. Army as a helicopter pilot and officer, including multiple deployments to Iraq, earning his Ranger tab.
Earned a master's degree from Harvard's Kennedy School and founded ScoutComms, a firm focused on veterans and military families.

Helped lead a team of Special Operations medical veterans to build and run a field hospital in New York City during the COVID-19 pandemic, and later served as Senior Advisor and Executive Director of the Lincoln Project.

priorities.text: Affordability: says families face rising costs for housing, healthcare, childcare and groceries while wages stay flat, and calls for lowering costs and expanding good-paying jobs.
Healthcare: supports a public option and allowing people to buy into Medicare before age 65 to increase competition and lower premiums.
Retirement security: wants to protect Social Security and Medicare and defend pensions.

positions.summary: Supports expanding access to affordable healthcare through a public option and allowing Missourians to buy into Medicare before turning 65.
Calls for immediately raising the federal minimum wage.
positions.quote: We must immediately raise the federal minimum wage

positions.summary: Says Congress must exercise its constitutional war powers and that the Iran conflict lacks congressional authorization.
positions.quote: Congress must exercise its constitutional war powers, demand clear objectives and accountability, and pursue serious diplomacy.

candidates.researchNotes: No prior elected office; positions drawn from his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey and campaign website.

candidates.name: Brandon Daugherty
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced unopposed in the August 4, 2026 Libertarian primary

summary.text: Brandon Daugherty is the Libertarian Party nominee for Missouri's 2nd District.

priorities.text: Free markets, limited government and a non-interventionist foreign policy.
priorities.quote: I support free markets, limited government, and a non-interventionist foreign policy, emphasizing personal freedom and voluntary interactions for economic and societal prosperity.

priorities.text: Bring U.S. troops home from overseas.
priorities.quote: My vision for America includes bringing all troops home from overseas.

priorities.text: Reduce regulation and shrink or eliminate federal agencies.
priorities.quote: I will advocate for less government regulations and fight to shrink or eliminate as many three letter agencies as possible.

positions.summary: Pledged on his 2024 campaign website not to vote for any legislation that restricts gun ownership for law-abiding Americans.
positions.quote: I promise not to vote for or endorse ANY legislation that restricts gun ownership for law-abiding Americans.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and priorities come from his 2024 campaign website as reproduced on Ballotpedia; he has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey (he did in 2024) and no current campaign website was found. Statements are dated 2024. No stated position found on abortion, taxes on high earners, health coverage or most other guide issues.

statements.quote: I will lead the charge on reforming immigration to bring back Ellis Island standards with increased points of entry and immediate access to green cards once a background check is cleared.
statements.context: From his 2024 campaign website, as reproduced on Ballotpedia
